title: The Michael Scott Invitational
logline: Michael takes the office bowling for a team-building outing where he hopes to be the center of attention, while Jim shows up with a date and Pam can't tell why it bothers her.
outline: A: Michael stages an Office Outing bowling tournament at Lackawanna Lanes; Jim brings a date, Shannon, and Pam is jealous and unsure why. B: Dwight and Andy are forced to share a client, Lenny Zorn of Lackawanna Lanes, and win him by luck. C: Kevin and Oscar notice Angela and Dwight arriving together; Angela thanks Dwight in public at the lanes. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, A, C, A, A, B, tag. (Reordered to alternate: cold, A, B, C, A, B, A, C, A, A, B, tag.)
theme: Being seen: everyone at the lanes wants someone to watch them win, and the people who watch the most are the ones who are looking away.
storySoFar: Michael still chases Jan's approval and David Wallace's praise; Stanley's countdown is at 202. Michael's Things I Love board holds Dwight's 61%, Kevin's M&Ms note and Dale Pruitt's card, plus Pam's drawing of Michael running. Jim and Pam keep circling a confession; Jim has tried several times and been interrupted, and Pam has noticed. Jim has now brought a date, Shannon Doyle, to the company's Office Outing at Lackawanna Lanes. Roy cancelled again by text. Dwight is Acting RM by his own memo and in an armed truce with Andy; they were forced to share a bowling-alley client, Lenny Zorn. Kevin and Oscar suspect Angela and Dwight's secret, and nobody says anything.

extras.name: Shannon Doyle
extras.title: Physical Therapist
extras.voice: Warm, direct, unbothered by Michael. Says exactly what she thinks, kindly. Likes Jim and is not intimidated by anyone at Dunder Mifflin. Notices things.

extras.name: Lenny Zorn
extras.title: Manager, Lackawanna Lanes
extras.voice: Tired, sweaty, bowling-alley realist. Wants his machines to work and his lanes to be full. Speaks in short complaints and then unexpected generosity.

stateChanges.status: dating, bringing her to the outing; Pam unsettled

stateChanges.arc: Will They, Won't They: Jim and Pam
stateChanges.progress: Jim brings Shannon to the Office Outing to make Pam jealous or to move on; Pam is jealous and unsure why. Jim tries to say something in the parking lot and is cut off by Shannon. Still unsaid.
Michael's Office Outing tournament is a bid for the whole office to cheer for him; Kevin cheers first and the office follows.
Forced to share Lenny Zorn; they win the account by luck when Lenny's scoring printer only takes Dunder paper. Dwight keeps the title, Andy keeps the crowd.
Angela thanks Dwight in public again at the lanes; Kevin and Oscar still suspect and say nothing.

stateChanges.text: Lenny Zorn's Lackawanna Lanes now uses Dunder paper for scoring sheets; Dwight had a plaque made.
Michael's Michael Scott Invitational trophy is a bowling pin spray-painted gold.
Stanley's countdown: 202 in the cold open, 201 in the tag; Michael's 'That's what she said' lands on silence.
Kevin: 'Nobody say nothing.' Used in the cold open and the tag.

scenes.recap: Stanley hits 202 days and Michael's joke dies, while Kevin hides his M&Ms.

beats.caption: sits at table_1 with a crossword and a sigh

beats.text: Stanley, you are two hundred and two days from freedom. That's what she said.

beats.caption: silence

beats.text: Two hundred and two.

beats.caption: tucks a family-size bag of M&Ms behind his back

beats.text: Kevin, are you hiding candy from your regional manager?
Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Michael announces the Office Outing bowling tournament, and Jim reveals he is bringing a plus-one.

beats.text: Team, this Friday we are going bowling at Lackawanna Lanes. It's the Michael Scott Invitational.
Question: is bowling a sport? False.
Plus-ones! Bring a plus-one. It's a party. Everybody's got a plus-one.
Plus-ones are a dead model. We're doing guest-first now.
I'm bringing someone.
Who?
Shannon.
Shannon who? Is she a Shannon I know? Is she in the Shannon union?

lines: Michael's trophy is a bowling pin he spray-painted gold. He told us that like it was a secret.
Shannon is a physical therapist. She's nice. She has no idea who Pam is, which is the point.

beats.text: Well, the trophy is going to be me, so nobody lose on purpose.

beats.caption: awkward silence

beats.text: Michael, the Party Planning Committee has not approved a bowling party.

scenes.recap: Michael assigns Dwight and Andy to share the Lackawanna Lanes account and Andy's banjo hold music interrupts.

beats.text: Dwight, Andy, you two are going to share Lenny Zorn at Lackawanna Lanes. Like brothers.
False. I share nothing. I am Acting Regional Manager.
Let's make this a Cornell-level collaboration, Dwight. Two minds, one scoring sheet.
Question: why does your phone have a bear paw?

beats.caption: holds up a bear-paw phone; banjo hold music starts ringing

beats.text: Actually, that's a banjo on hold.
It's a banjo on hold, Oscar. Thank you.
Okay, this is what a team looks like. Dwight, you have the scoring sheets. Andy, you have the banjo.
Acting Regional Manager approves the banjo for one hour.

scenes.recap: Kevin notices Angela and Dwight arrived at the same time, and Oscar refuses to discuss it.

beats.text: Angela and Dwight. Same car. Same time.
Actually, they came in separately. Angela took the Honda, Dwight took the beet truck.
Same time.

beats.caption: awkward silence

beats.text: Kevin, I am not going to discuss Angela's personal life in the break room.

lines: I'm an accountant. I don't speculate. I just know things.
Angela thanked Dwight for checking the fax, in front of everyone, and nobody has asked why she needed the fax checked.

beats.text: Fax machine was fine.
Yes. Kevin. That's what I'm saying.

scenes.recap: Pam reads Roy's cancellation text and asks about Shannon, and Jim says she is nice.

beats.text: Roy says he can't come Friday. Forklift, babe, sorry, sucks.
Oh. That's a shame.
He said that about the art show too.
So who's Shannon?
She's a physical therapist. I met her when I hurt my back carrying your sketchbook.
That was a month ago.
It was a very heavy sketchbook.

lines: I'm happy for Jim. He deserves someone who shows up.
I'm not sure why I put my pen down so hard when he said her name. It's a nice pen.

beats.text: Shannon! Shannon is a great name. Shannon is the name of a yacht.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy ride together to Lackawanna Lanes, and Andy's humming turns into a debate.

beats.text: Front seat is for the Acting Regional Manager. Back seat is for the banjo.

beats.caption: climbs into the passenger seat with his banjo case on his knees

beats.text: Dwight, we are on the same team. Can we agree on one thing? The Lenny Zorn account?
Question: what is the one thing?
We both want Lenny to like us more than the other guy.
False. Lenny will like me more. I have a beet-based pitch.

lines: I went to Cornell. I learned to share a stage, a table, and a bed with four strangers and a goose.
Dwight's car smells like beets and a bear, and I don't know which one is the Regional Manager.

beats.caption: turns the car radio to Battlestar Galactica theme; Andy hums along quietly

beats.text: You know this song?
Everybody knows this song. It is about a battle.

scenes.recap: The office arrives at the lanes; Jim walks in with Shannon and Pam meets her.

beats.text: Team! Welcome to the Michael Scott Invitational! Lanes one through eight are ours.
Hi. You're the boss who put the flyer on the dumpster.
That was a strategic placement.
It was next to a sign that said 'Free Kittens.'
Pam, this is Shannon.
Hi, Shannon. I'm Pam.
Oh! You're the artist. Jim showed me your sticky-note Dwight. He laughed for ten minutes.
He did.

beats.caption: looks for a bowling ball that is not her own

beats.text: Jim, Party Planning rules say guests sign in at the desk. Not the bar.
Did I stutter? We are at a bowling alley.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy pitch Lenny Zorn and lose until his scoring printer jams and only Dunder paper fits.

beats.text: Two of you. I wanted one paper guy. I got a fan club.
Question: which of us is the Acting Regional Manager? I am.
And I'm the sales guy with the crowd. Lenny, let me sing you the Dunder Mifflin—
No singing. My lanes are a hostage situation already.

beats.caption: unrolls a laminated chart of paper weights

beats.text: Is that a chart or a threat?
It is both. Dunder paper has a sixty-pound scoring weight.

beats.caption: slaps the side of a jammed scoring printer; it spits out a tangle of paper

beats.text: Printer's been eating every sheet since Easter. Nothing fits.

beats.caption: pulls a sample box from his bag; it is the exact size the printer needs

beats.text: Sixty-pound, eleven by seventeen. It's a Cornell thing. We carry extras.
Huh. That fits.
This was not a strategy. This was luck.
Luck is a Cornell value.
False.
Fine. You two bowl me one frame, I'll sign the paper.
Acting Regional Manager bowls for the team. Andy, you're up.

scenes.recap: Angela publicly thanks Dwight for checking the shoe rental sizes, and Kevin and Oscar both say nothing.

beats.text: Dwight, thank you for checking the shoe sizes. Publicly. Like a professional.
Acting Regional Manager checks everything. Including shoes.
Your shoe is a size eleven, Dwight. Mine is a seven. We are not the same.

beats.caption: awkward silence

beats.text: Same shoe, though.
Kevin. We are not saying anything.

beats.caption: chews an M&M very slowly and says nothing else

beats.text: Question: why is everyone looking at the shoe rack?
Nobody is looking at anything, Dwight. Bowl.

scenes.recap: The tournament climaxes: Shannon bowls a strike, Pam gutters, and Michael's speech falls flat until Kevin cheers for him.

beats.text: Ladies and gentlemen, I want to thank the people who came. Nobody had to.

beats.caption: quiet, then a single bowling ball rolls
bowls a perfect strike down lane three

beats.text: Ha! Sorry, Michael, I'm very competitive.

beats.caption: high-fives Shannon with a grin
rolls her ball into the gutter, eyes on the lane three cheering

beats.text: Gutter. Great. Good for her.
Michael Scott, the people's champion, bowls a seven. Let's go, team, give me a MI-KE!

beats.caption: nobody chants

beats.text: Michael!
Actually, the scoring sheet is in Dwight's favor for three frames.
Michael. Michael. There. Happy?
You know, I'd say that's the nicest thing anyone's ever said to me in a bowling alley.
Two of you signed the paper. Can I get a pitcher?

lines: I don't know why it's a gutter ball that makes me feel like that.
Shannon is nice. Jim is nice. It's not my job to be happy about it.

scenes.recap: Pam asks Jim why he brought Shannon, and Jim starts to say something before Shannon interrupts.

beats.text: Why did you bring her, Jim?
Because you said Roy wasn't coming, and I thought if I—
If you what?
Pam, I've been trying to say something since—
Jim! Michael says there's a team photo and he wants you in the middle with the pin.
Yeah. Okay.

beats.caption: Jim looks at Pam; Pam looks at the parking lot

beats.text: Go. Be in the middle. It's a nice pin.

lines: He tries to say something every time. And every time, someone needs a photo.
I'm not jealous. I just don't know what I'd do if he finished the sentence.

scenes.recap: Back at the office, Lenny's signed paper arrives and Dwight and Andy argue over who closed it.

beats.caption: holds up a signed Lackawanna Lanes paper order with a bowling-pin stamp

beats.text: Acting Regional Manager closed the Lenny Zorn account.
With a sixty-pound sample box and a Cornell value.
False. I had the chart.
You both did it! It's a team! You're like a two-headed bowling pin!
Did I stutter? Sign the paper and go home.
Dwight, I think we should sing a little.
Acting RM vetoes singing. Except for the three-note fanfare.

scenes.recap: Stanley drops to 201 and Michael's callback lands on silence, while Kevin sticks to his line.

beats.caption: sits at table_2 with a crossword and a sigh

beats.text: Stanley, one day closer to the end. That's what she said.

beats.caption: silence

beats.text: Two hundred and one.
Nobody say nothing.
